column1: # capacity-saturation.tsv — detector D2 inventory (kills Bun regression Class 2a, oven-sh/bun#31503).
# Generated: 2026-07-12
# Gate: .port/tools/gates/check_capacity_saturation.sh
# Tests: crates/rustty-vt/tests/d2_capacity_saturation.rs
# Oracle: /Users/gael/projects/ghostty pinned @ 4749c4e9 (every zig_origin resolves against this pin).
# WHY THIS AUDIT EXISTS (Bun Class 2a):
#   A `ptrs[allocated]` write-then-increment off-by-one was a SILENT out-of-bounds
#   write in ReleaseFast Zig for years (oven-sh/bun#31503/#31504), but the naive Rust
#   twin HARD PANICS on the identical index. Zig's own `IntFittingRange(0, max + 1)`
#   already encoded the true capacity: the array length is derivable from the same
#   expression the monotonic counter's range implies (`IntFittingRange(0, max+1)` =>
#   `[T; MAX+1]`). So this is a ONE-TIME audited inventory of every fixed `[T; N]` +
#   monotonic write-then-increment counter pair in rustty-vt HOT code (CSI param
#   buffers, page capacities, kitty/apc quotas): for each, N is derived from the Zig
#   counter-range expression, the port is confirmed to match, and a
#   `<name>_capacity_saturation` #[test] drives the bounded store to (and one past)
#   its ceiling so any off-by-one is a RED test, never a shipped OOB.
# TRIAGE RULE (process, not script): a Rust panic in a saturation test where the
#   ghostty oracle "worked" => re-run the oracle under ReleaseSafe/Debug FIRST (R3);
#   ReleaseFast Zig silently tolerates the OOB the port correctly refuses. Only after
#   the oracle also faults under ReleaseSafe is the port's ceiling wrong.
# GATE CONTRACT (fail-closed, R5-clean — ADDITIVE, weakens nothing):
#   * TSV absent            => BLOCKED (exit 3, surfaced as a WARNING by ci.sh).
#   * a data row names NO test (col `test` empty)                  => RED (exit 1).
#   * a named test is not defined in the tree (`fn <name>` absent) => RED (exit 1).
#   * an array_site whose file does not exist                      => RED (exit 1).
#   The gate is a source-level check (no build needed); the tests themselves run in
#   the normal `cargo test --workspace` lane, where a bounds panic is a RED test.
# SCHEMA (7 tab-separated columns; comment lines start with '#'; blank lines ignored):
#   1 pair          short id for the [T;N]+counter pair
#   2 array_site    <repo-relative-file>:<line> of the fixed `[T; N]` declaration
#   3 counter_site  <repo-relative-file>:<line> of the write-then-increment counter store
#   4 N             the derived capacity N and how the counter-range expression implies it
#   5 zig_origin    ghostty path:line + the reference declaration this ports
#   6 test          name of the guarding `#[test] fn <name>_capacity_saturation` (must exist)
#   7 notes         write/guard order and the ceiling the test drives to
